description: News & events (market-intelligence P3, workstream A). Two compact CSVs, no document store: SEC Form 8-K structured metadata (item codes, dates, accession) as a pre-classified, legally-mandated event spine, plus GDELT article-volume/tone salience as intensity. News enters scenariogen as a NUMERIC feature with a citation (a clamped multiplier on the ARag idiosyncratic leg), never as retrieved text — the architectural guard against overload. See docs/design/AITrade_market_intelligence_design.md §2.
_six_k_rules_comment: Form 6-K (foreign private issuers, e.g. TSM) carries no item codes. Each 6-K maps to the 8-K item it is equivalent to by the FIRST rule whose regex matches its EDGAR primary-document file name (case-insensitive); item null = routine, dropped; no match = dropped, like an 8-K with no allowlisted item. The patterns follow TSM's own file naming, not an SEC taxonomy -- review them like the allowlist. docs/specs/sec-6k-events.md.

sec_company_tickers.name: SEC company_tickers.json — ticker→CIK map (A0)
sec_company_tickers.description: The authoritative SEC-published ticker→CIK map. A0 resolves the portfolio's 8-K filers to CIKs from this file, fails loud below the coverage floor, and drift-checks the result against the in-repo bond-issuer CIKs.

sec_events.name: SEC EDGAR 8-K item-code event stream (A1)
sec_events.description: Per-CIK submissions JSON, filtered to Form 8-K with allowlisted item codes. Structured metadata only (no NLP): item codes, filing dates, accession numbers, doc URLs. Requires a User-Agent with contact per SEC policy.

gdelt.name: GDELT 2.0 article-volume / tone salience (A2)
gdelt.description: Per-entity daily article volume + average tone with a historical series (timelinevolinfo / timelinetone), so vol/tone z-scores are available immediately without an accumulation wait. GDELT asks for one request every 5s.
